title: Draft critique — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Public knowledge about this ability, fact-checked reference. Public edition. Public knowledge about this ability, fact-checked reference. Draft critique is one of the actual creation abilitys an AI needs in order to write, program, create files, and build software. It is not a document category and not a program: it is an underlying capability of the AI itself. This database stores everything that supports the ability — the knowledge it rests on, the methods and algorithms, reusable components, specifications, worked examples, and the tests that show whether the ability is really present.

title: Draft critique — The four layers
body: Public edition. Public knowledge about this ability, fact-checked reference. Public edition. Public knowledge about this ability, fact-checked reference. Four layers: intelligence (understand, reason, plan), generation (produce language, code, files), execution (read/write files, run tools, compile, build), verification (test, repair, confirm). A database alone does not grant an ability: the system must actually be able to use the database's contents to perform the operation. These records store the knowledge, methods, algorithms, reusable components, specifications, and examples that support the ability, plus an implementation path showing what else is required. For draft critique, the intelligence layer covers recognizing when the ability is needed and planning its use. The generation layer covers producing the language, code, or structures the ability outputs. The execution layer covers performing the file, tool, and runtime operations the ability requires. The verification layer covers testing the result and repairing failures. The demo on this page maps each step of the ability to its layer, so gaps are visible.

Knowledge required for draft critique: the domain facts, terminology, and reference examples recorded in this database. Algorithm or procedure: the step-by-step method, demonstrated in the worked record. Executable tool: the programs or engines that perform the operation, invoked through a defined interface with permissions. Inputs and outputs: the contract each invocation must satisfy. Test: the demonstration that shows whether the ability works, executed at build time and recorded below.

title: Draft critique — Worked demonstration with verification test
body: Public edition. Public knowledge about this ability, fact-checked reference. Public edition. Public knowledge about this ability, fact-checked reference. Turning this catalog entry into a working ability takes four concrete artifacts. One: the knowledge in this database, queryable by the AI. Two: the procedure, encoded as the demo pipeline. Three: the execution binding — the file, tool, or runtime access the ability needs, with permissions checked. Four: the verification test, run here at build time and re-runnable later. Where any of the four is missing, the record says so plainly instead of pretending the ability is complete.

title: Draft critique — Limits and honest boundaries
body: Public edition. Public knowledge about this ability, fact-checked reference. Public edition. Public knowledge about this ability, fact-checked reference. Honest limits of draft critique. A database entry describing an ability does not install the ability: without the execution layer (file access, tool access, runtime), the ability is knowledge, not capability. The final demo proves the point constructively — it attempts the ability with the execution layer withheld and returns a structured refusal instead of a fake result. Genuine completion criteria: the ability runs end-to-end on real inputs, its tests pass, and its failures are diagnosed, not hidden.
